seoTitle: How to Use Google Workspace as a CRM with Streak & Copper
metaDescription: Learn how to turn Google Workspace into a CRM using Streak and Copper CRM, tracking leads and deals directly inside Gmail and Sheets.
intro: Rather than paying for a separate CRM platform, tools like Streak and Copper let you manage leads and client relationships directly inside the Google Workspace apps you already use. Both install through the Google Workspace Marketplace and hook straight into Gmail, so your pipeline lives next to the emails that actually move deals forward instead of in a browser tab you have to remember to check. This guide walks through finding both tools in the Marketplace, installing them the right way for your account type, and setting up a working sales pipeline in Streak so you can see how the Gmail-first approach actually feels day to day.

steps.heading: Find Streak and Copper in the Workspace Marketplace
steps.body: Open the Google Workspace Marketplace and search for the CRM you want — searching a partial name like "coo" for Copper surfaces the whole Sales & CRM category, including Streak, Salesforce Connector, and Zoho CRM alongside it, each with its install count and star rating visible before you commit. This is worth doing even if you already know which tool you want, since the category view makes it obvious how each one is positioned and rated relative to the others, and you can see at a glance whether a tool like Streak already shows as "Installed" on your account.

image.caption: The Workspace Marketplace's Sales & CRM results, with Streak already marked Installed alongside Salesforce Connector and Zoho CRM.

steps.heading: Install Copper the right way for your organization
steps.body: When you install Copper from the Marketplace, it asks whether you want an Admin install or an Individual install. Admin install rolls the app out to your entire Google Workspace organization, or to specific organizational units or groups you choose, and Google is upfront that this can take up to 24 hours to fully propagate across a domain. Individual install just adds it to your own account. Pick Admin install if you're setting this up for a team that needs shared pipeline visibility; pick Individual if you're the only one who'll use it for now.

image.caption: Copper's Marketplace install prompt, choosing between an org-wide Admin install and a single-user Individual install.

steps.heading: Let Streak set up inside your Gmail inbox
steps.body: Once Streak is added, it launches its onboarding directly inside Gmail rather than a separate app, with a brief "Analyzing your inbox" step before you land on your pipeline. You can skip this analysis if you'd rather start from a blank pipeline, or let it continue to get suggested setup based on your existing email activity. Either way, notice that Streak's whole interface lives as a panel inside Gmail itself — there's no separate CRM tab to switch to, which is the core of its pitch over a standalone tool.

image.caption: Streak's onboarding running inside Gmail, briefly analyzing the inbox before handing off to pipeline setup.

steps.heading: Build your first pipeline from a template
steps.body: Streak's pipeline creation screen offers templates for Sales, Projects, Business Dev, Hiring, Job Search, Investor, Fundraising, and more, each pre-loaded with stages that match that use case. The Sales template comes with Lead, Contacted, Pitched, Demo, Negotiating, Closed - Lost, Closed - Won, and Nurturing as color-coded stages, which you can rename, reorder, or delete once the pipeline exists. Starting from a template rather than a blank pipeline saves the setup time of deciding stage names from scratch, and you can always add a custom pipeline later for a workflow that doesn't fit the presets.

image.caption: Streak's Sales pipeline template, with color-coded stages from Lead through Closed - Won ready to customize before creating it.

steps.heading: Decide between Streak and Copper for your team
steps.body: Streak's strength is exactly what the setup shows — it never leaves Gmail, which makes it fast to adopt for a solopreneur or a two-person team that already lives in their inbox. Copper leans further into being a full CRM with its own dashboard, deeper Google Contacts and Calendar automation, and reporting built for a team that needs visibility across multiple pipelines and users. If your team is small and email-centric, start with Streak; if you're coordinating several people around shared deal data, Copper's admin-level install and structure will scale better.

steps.heading: Track leads and set up automated follow-ups
steps.body: With a pipeline in place, each email thread relevant to a deal gets added as a box you drag between stages, and both tools let you set reminders that surface automatically when a lead has gone quiet. This is where the CRM starts paying for itself — instead of relying on memory to know a lead hasn't heard back in a week, the tool resurfaces it in your inbox at the right time, which is the entire point of running a CRM through Gmail rather than a disconnected app.

steps.heading: Sync your data with Sheets and Contacts
steps.body: Both Streak and Copper offer export or live-sync options into Google Sheets, which is useful once you want to build a report or chart that the CRM's own dashboard doesn't cover. Copper's tighter Google Contacts integration also means client details you update in one place show up in the other, keeping a single source of truth for a customer's information instead of duplicating it across tools.

faq.question: Is Streak or Copper better for a small business?
faq.answer: Streak is often preferred by solopreneurs and small teams for its simplicity inside Gmail, while Copper suits businesses that need more advanced automation, admin-level rollout, and reporting.

faq.question: Do I need a separate CRM subscription to use these tools?
faq.answer: Yes, both Streak and Copper are third-party tools with their own pricing plans that integrate with, but are separate from, your Google Workspace subscription.

faq.question: Can I manage my entire sales pipeline without leaving Gmail?
faq.answer: Yes, that's the main appeal of Streak specifically — pipelines, deal tracking, and follow-ups can all be managed directly from a panel inside your Gmail inbox.

faq.question: What's the difference between an Admin install and an Individual install for Copper?
faq.answer: Admin install rolls the app out to your whole Google Workspace organization or selected groups, which can take up to 24 hours to finish; Individual install only adds it to your own account.

faq.question: Do Streak and Copper work with Google Calendar?
faq.answer: Yes, both integrate with Google Calendar and Contacts to help schedule and track follow-ups and appointments tied to your CRM pipeline.
